patient_actor_hidden.History: The patient reports a 2-month history of insidious onset left shoulder pain, worsening with extreme ranges of motion and activity. Pain disrupts sleep, and there's noted difficulty with activities of daily living like brushing hair and dressing. No history of shoulder trauma, neck pain, arm/hand weakness, numbness, or paresthesias. The patient has type 2 diabetes mellitus, treated with metformin and glipizide.

Secondary_Symptoms: Difficulty sleeping on the affected side
Difficulty with brushing hair and dressing

patient_actor_hidden.Review_of_Systems: Denies neck pain, arm/hand weakness, numbness, or paresthesias.

objective_for_doctor: Assess and diagnose the patient presenting with chronic left shoulder pain without a history of trauma.

turns.doctor_opening: Hello, what brings you in today? Could you tell me about yourself and what's been going on?
turns.patient_opening: “I’ve had left shoulder pain for about two months that slowly got worse, especially when I move it to extreme ranges or try to use it during activities. It also disrupts my sleep and makes daily tasks like brushing my hair and dressing pretty difficult. I haven’t had any shoulder injury, neck pain, or any numbness or weakness in my arm or hand.”

turns.doctor_question: Do you have any small, raised bumps on your skin that have a tiny indentation or a "dimple" in the center?
turns.patient_answer: “I haven’t noticed any small raised bumps on my skin, and I don’t recall seeing anything with a dimple in the center.”

turns.doctor_question: Have you noticed that you need to urinate more often than usual?
turns.patient_answer: “I don’t think I’ve been urinating more often than usual, and I haven’t noticed any new urinary symptoms.”

turns.doctor_question: Have you been feeling generally weak or lacking your usual strength lately?
turns.patient_answer: “I haven’t felt generally weak or lacking my usual strength. My main issue has been the left shoulder pain, especially with extreme movements and everyday tasks, and it’s been waking me up at night.”

turns.doctor_question: Have you noticed any rashes, bumps, or sores appearing specifically along the veins in your arms?
turns.patient_answer: “I haven’t noticed any rash, bumps, or sores along the veins in my arms—nothing like that has shown up. My concern has mainly been the persistent left shoulder pain, worse with extreme movement and activity, and it’s been bothering my sleep. I haven’t had any new skin changes that I’m aware of.”

turns.doctor_question: Have you been experiencing any itchiness on your skin?
turns.patient_answer: “No, I haven’t noticed any itchiness or new rashes or skin changes. My symptoms have been focused on the left shoulder pain—worse with extreme movement, affecting dressing and brushing my hair, and disrupting my sleep.”

turns.doctor_question: Do you experience any pain or cramping in your calves when you walk that goes away once you stop and rest?
turns.patient_answer: “No, I haven’t noticed any pain or cramping in my calves when I walk. My discomfort is mainly in my left shoulder, especially with extreme ranges of motion and during daily activities, and it’s been disrupting my sleep.”

turns.doctor_question: Have you noticed if your stools have become unusually pale, light-colored, or clay-colored recently?
turns.patient_answer: “No, I haven’t noticed any change in my stool color—nothing pale or clay-like. My only problem has been the persistent left shoulder pain that worsens with extreme movement and activity and interferes with sleep and daily tasks like dressing and brushing my hair.”

turns.doctor_question: Have you noticed any weakness in your hands, such as difficulty gripping objects or a tendency to drop things more often than usual?
turns.patient_answer: “No, I haven’t noticed any weakness in my hands, and I’m not dropping things more than usual. My difficulties are mainly with using my left shoulder because of the pain, especially at the extremes of motion.”

turns.doctor_question: During these shaking episodes, are you able to remain conscious and aware of your surroundings, or do you lose consciousness?
turns.patient_answer: “I haven’t had any shaking episodes, so I haven’t noticed whether I remain conscious or lose consciousness.”
